title: GPT-2
blurb: OpenAI's 2019 code and released weights for GPT-2. A real open-weight language model years before LLaMA, not a retroactive slogan.

title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
blurb: The GPT-2 paper. The PDF is the primary write-up; the GitHub repo is the code and weights.

title: GPT-Neo
blurb: EleutherAI's open GPT-3-style models and training code, from the period when the largest GPT-3 weights were not public.

title: GPT-J-6B
blurb: EleutherAI's 6B model, Apache-2.0 on the Hub, and the model a lot of 2021-2022 open tooling actually ran.

title: Mesh Transformer JAX
blurb: The JAX code used to train GPT-J. The weights live on the Hub; this is the training implementation.

title: GPT-NeoX
blurb: EleutherAI's distributed training library, used for GPT-NeoX and Pythia. Still a reference pretraining stack, not just a 2022 artifact.

title: OPT-66B
blurb: Meta's 2022 66B decoder. Weights are downloadable under a research license, not Apache-2.0 or MIT.

title: Metaseq
blurb: The codebase Meta published with OPT. The models are open-weight research releases, not an OSI-licensed family.

title: BLOOM
blurb: BigScience's 176B multilingual model. The Hub license is the BigScience RAIL, which adds use restrictions on top of the weight release.

title: Pythia
blurb: EleutherAI's suite of models trained on the same data in the same order so training dynamics can be studied. Code and weights are Apache-2.0.

title: Introducing LLaMA
blurb: Meta's February 2023 research release (7B to 65B). Access was gated and non-commercial; it still became the base of the first public fine-tune wave.

title: Llama
blurb: Meta's Llama model repo (the old facebookresearch/llama URL redirects here). Weights are under the Llama community licenses, not Apache-2.0.

title: Llama 2
blurb: July 2023 release with a custom community license that allowed commercial use under its conditions. Meta called it open source; the license is not OSI-approved.

title: Llama 3.1
blurb: Meta's July 2024 post for the 8B, 70B, and 405B models with a 128K context. Same community-license pattern as Llama 3, not an Apache grant.

title: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
blurb: The practical small Llama 3.1 checkpoint. Hub license field is llama3.1, a custom community license.

title: Llama 4 Scout
blurb: Meta's 2025 open-weight multimodal MoE (17B active). Hub license is the custom Llama license, which Meta itself now describes as open-weight rather than open source.

title: Llama 4 Maverick
blurb: The larger Llama 4 MoE sibling of Scout, also multimodal and under the same custom license.

title: Llama developer docs
blurb: Current Meta docs for the Llama weights and prompt formats. The marketing site and this doc host are both first-party; the license text is still the community license.

title: Mistral 7B
blurb: Mistral's September 2023 announcement of a 7.3B model under Apache-2.0. This is the release that made a permissive commercial self-host realistic at laptop size.

title: Mistral-7B-v0.1
blurb: The original Apache-2.0 checkpoint. Later instruct and v0.3 weights exist; this card is the one the 2023 announcement pointed at.

title: Mixtral of experts
blurb: December 2023 announcement of Mixtral 8x7B, the sparse MoE that made open mixture-of-experts normal. Apache-2.0.

title: Mixtral-8x7B-v0.1
blurb: Apache-2.0 weights for Mixtral 8x7B. About 47B parameters stored, with far fewer active per token.

title: Pixtral 12B
blurb: Mistral's first natively multimodal open model, Apache-2.0 on the Hub. A 12B decoder plus a vision encoder, not a text model with a bolted-on captioner.

title: Magistral Small
blurb: Apache-2.0 reasoning model (24B). Magistral Medium stayed API-only; this card is the open one.

title: Devstral Small
blurb: Apache-2.0 agentic coding model Mistral released with All Hands. It is a fine-tune line, not a general chat replacement.

title: Mistral Large 3
blurb: Apache-2.0 sparse MoE, 675B total, from the December 2025 Mistral 3 family. Earlier Mistral Large 2 used a research license; this generation's card says Apache-2.0.

title: Mistral Small 4
blurb: Mistral's announcement of one Apache-2.0 model meant to cover instruct, reasoning, and coding, instead of three separate checkpoints.

title: Mistral Small 4 119B
blurb: The Apache-2.0 weights: a 119B MoE with multimodal input. The card is the artifact; the news post is the framing.

title: mistral-inference
blurb: Official reference inference code for Mistral models. Production serving usually goes through vLLM or llama.cpp instead.

title: Qwen
blurb: First-generation Qwen repo. Those early weights used the Tongyi Qianwen license; the code was Apache-2.0. Later generations changed the weight license.

title: Qwen3
blurb: Repo and release notes for Qwen3. From this generation the Qwen team states that the open-weight models are Apache-2.0.

title: Qwen3 blog
blurb: The Qwen3 launch post: hybrid thinking and non-thinking modes, and the Apache-2.0 claim for the open weights.

title: Qwen3-235B-A22B
blurb: Apache-2.0 Qwen3 mixture-of-experts, 235B total and 22B active. A flagship of that generation, not the 2026 line.

title: QwQ-32B
blurb: Apache-2.0 open reasoning model from the Qwen team. The preview that started this line was November 2024; this card is the 32B release.

title: Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B
blurb: Apache-2.0 agentic code MoE, 480B total and 35B active. A specialist checkpoint, not the general Qwen3 chat model.

title: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B
blurb: Apache-2.0 vision-language MoE. Hub repo created 2026-02-16, the first size in the Qwen3.5 line.

title: Qwen3.6-27B
blurb: Apache-2.0 dense vision-language model. Hub repo created 2026-04-21. The Qwen3.6 GitHub name now redirects to the Qwen3.8 repo.

title: Qwen3.8
blurb: Canonical GitHub repo for Qwen3.5, Qwen3.6, and Qwen3.8. Read the license per checkpoint: the 27B is Apache-2.0 and the 2.4T card is not.

title: Qwen3.8-27B
blurb: Apache-2.0 dense vision-language model, Hub repo created 2026-08-05. The size people actually download for a single GPU.

title: Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B
blurb: Open-weight text MoE, Hub repo created 2026-08-08. The license field is custom, not Apache-2.0, unlike the 27B.

title: Gemma
blurb: Google DeepMind's Gemma page. Gemma 1 through 3 shipped under the Gemma Terms of Use; Gemma 4 is the generation that moved to Apache-2.0.

title: Gemma reference code
blurb: Official Gemma model code. Inference for real deployments is usually llama.cpp, vLLM, MLX, or the cookbook, not this repo alone.

title: Gemma 3 27B Instruct
blurb: Vision-language Gemma 3 checkpoint. Hub license is gemma, the older terms, not Apache-2.0.

title: Gemma 4
blurb: Google's Gemma 4 announcement. The post says this generation is Apache-2.0, which the Hub license fields for the 31B, 26B-A4B, and E4B cards match.

title: Gemma 4 31B
blurb: Apache-2.0 dense vision-language Gemma 4. Hub repo created 2026-03-11.

title: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
blurb: Apache-2.0 Gemma 4 mixture-of-experts. Fewer parameters active per token than the 31B dense model, so it is the faster of the two mid sizes.

title: Gemma 4 E4B
blurb: Apache-2.0 edge Gemma 4. The Hub pipeline tag is any-to-any, which is the small multimodal checkpoint rather than the text-only 31B.

title: Gemma cookbook
blurb: Official notebooks for running and fine-tuning Gemma, including the Apache-2.0 Gemma 4 weights.

title: DeepSeek LLM
blurb: DeepSeek's first open models (2023). Code in that era was MIT; the weight license was the DeepSeek model license, not yet the MIT weights of R1.

title: DeepSeek-V2
blurb: The 2024 MoE that introduced Multi-head Latent Attention. A research and architecture landmark more than a checkpoint you would pick in 2026.

title: DeepSeek-V3
blurb: 671B-total MoE release repo (December 2024). Later DeepSeek weight releases moved to MIT; read this repo's license instead of assuming that backward.

title: DeepSeek-R1
blurb: January 2025 reasoning model and the distilled smaller checkpoints, released under MIT. The repo that made open reasoning weights ordinary.

title: DeepSeek-V4 preview
blurb: DeepSeek's 24 April 2026 post announcing open V4-Pro and V4-Flash weights with a 1M-token context.

title: DeepSeek-V4 on Hugging Face
blurb: Hugging Face's 24 April 2026 write-up of the V4 checkpoints, including which repos are instruct versus base.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
blurb: MIT-licensed text MoE. Hub repo created 2026-04-22. The large V4 checkpoint, not the Flash line.

title: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731
blurb: MIT-licensed text checkpoint, Hub repo created 2026-07-31. A later Flash build than the April preview repo.

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
blurb: MIT-licensed multimodal model, Hub repo created 2026-09-10. The newest DeepSeek weight repo confirmed for this ingest.

title: Olmo
blurb: AllenAI's fully open language-model project: weights, training data, and code, which is a stricter bar than open weights alone.

title: OLMo code
blurb: Training and inference code for OLMo. Apache-2.0, and the repo that goes with the Dolma data.

title: OLMo 2 13B
blurb: Apache-2.0 OLMo 2 base model. A fully open 13B from the November 2024 line, before Olmo 3.

title: Olmo 3
blurb: Ai2's write-up of the 7B and 32B Olmo 3 family, including the Think variants whose reasoning traces they tie back to the training data.

title: Olmo 3.1 Think 32B
blurb: Apache-2.0 thinking model. Hub repo created 2025-12-10. Fully open weights, not a Llama-license clone.

title: Apertus 70B Instruct
blurb: Apache-2.0 70B instruct model from the Swiss AI Initiative. Hub repo created 2025-09-01.

title: Marin
blurb: Open training stack aimed at reproducing modern language models with public data and code, in the same spirit as OLMo rather than a closed pretrain.

title: gpt-oss
blurb: OpenAI's open-weight model repo. The 20B and 120B checkpoints on the Hub are Apache-2.0. The openai.com announcement page blocked this ingest, so the repo and cards are the cited sources.

title: gpt-oss-20b
blurb: Apache-2.0 MoE reasoning model sized to run locally. Hub repo created 2025-08-04.

title: gpt-oss-120b
blurb: Apache-2.0 larger gpt-oss checkpoint. Hub repo created 2025-08-04. Open weights from OpenAI, not a leaked model.

title: gpt-oss-safeguard-20b
blurb: Apache-2.0 safety classifier that reasons over a policy you supply. Hub repo created 2025-09-18.

title: Phi-2
blurb: Microsoft's 2.7B model under MIT. The small-model result that made Phi a line rather than a paper.

title: Phi-4
blurb: MIT-licensed 14B model. Microsoft's data-quality pitch, with weights you can actually download.

title: Phi-4-reasoning
blurb: MIT-licensed reasoning variant of Phi-4. Hub repo created 2025-04-09.

title: Phi cookbook
blurb: Microsoft's notebooks for the Phi models, including the MIT-licensed open weights.

title: Yi-34B
blurb: 01.AI's 34B model. Hub license is Apache-2.0. The 2023-2024 bilingual line, not a 2026 flagship.

title: Granite 3.3 8B Instruct
blurb: Apache-2.0 IBM Granite instruct model. Hub repo created 2025-04-09.

title: Grok-1
blurb: JAX code for xAI's 314B MoE. The README in this repo says the code and the Grok-1 weights are Apache-2.0, and it points at a magnet link plus a Hub download.

title: GLM-5.3-Flash
blurb: MIT-licensed multimodal GLM from Z.ai. Hub repo created 2026-08-25. The full GLM-5.3 card is a different, custom license.

title: GLM-5
blurb: Z.ai's repo covering GLM-5 through GLM-5.3. Use it to see which sibling is MIT (Flash) and which is the custom-license flagship.

title: Hy4 preview
blurb: Apache-2.0 text model from Tencent's Hy team. Hub repo created 2026-08-27. The card describes a 770B-total MoE preview, not a general Hunyuan product page.

title: SmolLM3 3B
blurb: Apache-2.0 3B model from Hugging Face. Hub repo created 2025-07-08. Small on purpose.

title: SmolLM
blurb: Training and data recipes for the SmolLM series, including SmolLM3. Apache-2.0 models with the corpus work published alongside.

title: Command R+
blurb: Cohere's Command R+ weights. Hub license is CC BY-NC 4.0, so commercial use is not granted.

title: Aya Expanse 32B
blurb: Cohere For AI's multilingual model. Hub license is CC BY-NC 4.0, the same non-commercial limit as Command R+.

title: DBRX
blurb: Databricks' March 2024 announcement of a 132B MoE. The weight host asked this ingest for authorization, so the public citation is the announcement, not a silent Hub mirror.

title: Falcon 180B
blurb: TII's 180B model. The Hub card does not expose a standard SPDX license id; read the license file on the card before commercial use.

title: GLM-5.3
blurb: Z.ai's text flagship. Hub license is custom, not the MIT license used by GLM-5.3-Flash. Hub repo created 2026-08-25.

title: Kimi K2
blurb: Moonshot's Kimi K2 code and release repo. Later Kimi K3 weights are a separate card with their own license.

title: Kimi K3
blurb: Open-weight multimodal model, Hub license name kimi-k3 (custom, not Apache or MIT). Hub repo created 2026-06-13.

title: Nemotron 70B Instruct
blurb: NVIDIA's instruct tune of Llama 3.1 70B. Hub license is llama3.1, so the Llama community terms still apply.

title: OpenELM 3B
blurb: Apple's 3B open-weight model. Hub license is the Apple AMLR research license, not Apache-2.0.

title: OpenELM paper page
blurb: Apple's research page for OpenELM. The weights are public; the license is Apple's, not an OSI license.

title: LFM2-8B-A1B
blurb: Liquid AI's 8B mixture model. Hub license is custom. Hub repo created 2025-10-07.

title: StarCoder2 15B
blurb: BigCode's 15B code model. Hub license is BigCode OpenRAIL-M, which is a responsible-use license, not plain Apache-2.0.

title: StarCoder2
blurb: The StarCoder2 release repo. Pair it with the model card so the OpenRAIL-M terms are not missed.

title: StableLM 2 12B
blurb: Stability AI's 12B model. The Hub license field is a custom Stability license, not Apache-2.0.

title: StableLM
blurb: Stability's language-model repo. Check the checkpoint license; the org name is not a license.

title: InternLM
blurb: Shanghai AI Lab's InternLM code and model line. Treat the license on the checkpoint you download as the license, not this README's tone.

title: MiniCPM
blurb: OpenBMB's small-model line, aimed at edge devices. Confirm the license file in the version you pull.

title: Hunyuan-A13B
blurb: Tencent's earlier Hunyuan-A13B MoE. Hy4 preview is the newer Apache-2.0 Hy release; this repo is the prior line.

title: OpenHands
blurb: Open-source software-engineering agent that drives a shell, editor, and browser against whatever model you point it at, including a local server.

title: smolagents
blurb: Hugging Face's small agent library. It is code-agent shaped and runs against local model servers, not a hosted product.

title: AutoGen
blurb: Microsoft's multi-agent framework. Model calls go through an OpenAI-compatible client, so a local runtime can sit behind it.

title: Pydantic AI
blurb: Typed agent library from the Pydantic team. Useful when the model is local and you still want structured tool calls.

title: browser-use
blurb: Python library that lets a model drive a real browser. It does not ship a model; you bring an open one.

title: Open Interpreter
blurb: Local-first interpreter that lets a model run code on your machine. Point it at Ollama or llama.cpp rather than assuming a hosted default.

title: goose
blurb: Open-source extensible agent from the goose project (the block/goose URL redirects here). It installs, edits, and runs code against any configured LLM.

title: CrewAI
blurb: Role-based multi-agent library. Open code; the model is whichever server you configure.

title: LangGraph
blurb: Graph runtime for agent workflows from the LangChain team. Open source library, not a weight release.

title: GPT Researcher
blurb: Autonomous research agent that plans a query, reads pages, and writes a report. Swap the model endpoint for a local one.

title: STORM
blurb: Stanford's open research agent for writing Wikipedia-style articles with citations. A research system, not a hosted writer.

title: Aider
blurb: Terminal pair-programmer that edits a git repo. It speaks to any OpenAI-compatible server, including a local open model.

title: Continue
blurb: Open-source IDE extension for chat and edits. Local models via Ollama and llama.cpp are a documented path, not an afterthought.

title: Cline
blurb: Open-source VS Code coding agent that can run commands in the workspace. You choose the model, including local endpoints.

title: Roo Code
blurb: Open-source fork of the Cline-style coding agent, with its own modes. Same caveat: the model is not bundled.

title: OpenCode
blurb: Open-source coding agent (the sst/opencode URL redirects here). A terminal UI, not a weight release.

title: Tabby
blurb: Self-hosted code completion server. It serves open code models; it is not a closed Copilot clone with a key.

title: Void
blurb: Open-source editor forked toward local and self-hosted models. The editor is the product; you still pick the weights.

title: LlamaIndex
blurb: Data framework for retrieval on top of an LLM. The name is historical; it is not tied to Meta's license.

title: Haystack
blurb: Open pipeline library for retrieval and question answering. Local generators are a normal backend.

title: RAGFlow
blurb: Open RAG engine with document parsing and a UI. Aimed at self-hosting, including open models.

title: Dify
blurb: Open app builder for RAG and agents. You can point the model provider at a local OpenAI-compatible server.

title: AnythingLLM
blurb: Desktop and server app for chatting with your documents through Ollama, LM Studio, or another local backend.

title: PrivateGPT
blurb: The early local-document QA app. Still a clear example of RAG that never sends the prompt to a hosted model.

title: Khoj
blurb: Self-hosted personal research assistant over your notes and documents, with local model support.

title: Docling
blurb: Document parser that turns PDFs and office files into structured text for a RAG index. It is not itself a language model.

title: Sentence Transformers
blurb: The usual open library for embedding models that sit in front of an open generator.

title: FlagEmbedding
blurb: BAAI's embedding and reranker code, including BGE. Open retrieval models, used next to open generators.

title: GraphRAG
blurb: Microsoft's open graph-based retrieval pipeline. It calls a model you configure; the graph step is the point.

title: SillyTavern
blurb: Front end for local roleplay and character chat. It connects to koboldcpp, llama.cpp, Ollama, and similar backends.

title: Hugging Face Chat UI
blurb: Open chat interface used by HuggingChat. You can run it against your own text-generation server.

title: koboldcpp
blurb: Single-file llama.cpp distribution aimed at story and roleplay front ends. A runtime and a creative app at once.

title: PocketPal AI
blurb: Mobile app that runs GGUF models on-device through llama.cpp. The weights are whatever you download into it.

title: exo
blurb: Runs a model across a cluster of home machines. An open runtime for machines you already own, not a cloud product.

title: WebLLM
blurb: Runs open models in the browser with WebGPU. In-browser weights, not a call to a vendor API.

title: DSPy
blurb: Stanford's framework for programming language models instead of hand-writing prompts. Works with local model clients.

title: Outlines
blurb: Constrained decoding so a model emits JSON or a regex. The outlines-dev URL redirects here.

title: Instructor
blurb: Pydantic structured output on top of model APIs, including local OpenAI-compatible servers.

title: Guidance
blurb: Constraint and templating library for generation. Useful when an open model has to follow a format.

title: LLMs from Scratch
blurb: Sebastian Raschka's book-style repo that implements a GPT, then trains and fine-tunes it, in readable PyTorch.

title: TransformerLens
blurb: Mechanistic-interpretability library for looking inside decoder models, including open checkpoints.

title: SAELens
blurb: Sparse-autoencoder tooling for open models. The jbloomAus/SAELens URL redirects here.

title: Candle
blurb: Hugging Face's Rust tensor library, with LLM examples. A minimal runtime, not a serving stack.

title: ExLlamaV2
blurb: GPU inference for EXL2 quantizations of open models. Faster than a naive Transformers load, narrower than vLLM.

title: ik_llama.cpp
blurb: A llama.cpp fork focused on quantization and CPU/GPU kernels. Use it when mainline GGUF is not enough; it is not the upstream project.

title: llama.cpp
blurb: C and C++ inference for GGUF models on CPU and GPU. The ggerganov/llama.cpp URL redirects here. This is the default local runtime.

title: llamafile
blurb: Runs an open model as a single executable file. The Mozilla-Ocho URL redirects here.

title: LMDeploy
blurb: InternLM's serving toolkit for compressed open models, with a TurboMind backend. Not limited to InternLM weights.

title: MLC LLM
blurb: Compiles open models onto native and browser runtimes. The engine behind a lot of on-device and WebGPU demos.

title: MLX LM
blurb: Apple's MLX library for running and fine-tuning language models on Apple silicon.

title: ONNX Runtime GenAI
blurb: Microsoft's generative runtime on top of ONNX Runtime, used for Windows and on-device open models.

title: SGLang
blurb: Serving runtime for open models, often faster than a stock vLLM setup on the same GPU. Open code.

title: TabbyAPI
blurb: OpenAI-compatible server in front of ExLlamaV2. A server, not a model.

title: TensorRT-LLM
blurb: NVIDIA's open compiler and runtime for LLM inference on its GPUs. Apache-2.0 code; it runs open weights, it is not a weight license.

title: Text Generation Inference
blurb: Hugging Face's production serving stack for Hub models. Open code, aimed at GPU servers rather than laptops.

title: vLLM
blurb: The common open serving engine for open weights: paged attention, continuous batching, and an OpenAI-compatible API.

title: GPT4All
blurb: Desktop app for running local chat models, plus its own historically released small models. The app is the reason to list it.

title: Jan
blurb: Open-source desktop app for downloading and chatting with local models.

title: llama-cpp-python
blurb: Python bindings for llama.cpp, including an OpenAI-compatible server. Bindings, not a new engine.

title: LiteLLM
blurb: A proxy that presents many backends, including Ollama and vLLM, as one OpenAI-compatible API.

title: LM Studio
blurb: Desktop app for running local models. The app itself is not open source; the open pieces are the lms CLI and mlx-engine repos.

title: lms
blurb: Open CLI for LM Studio. This repo is not the closed desktop shell.

title: mlx-engine
blurb: Open MLX inference engine used by LM Studio on Apple silicon.

title: LocalAI
blurb: OpenAI-compatible server that wraps local models, including llama.cpp backends. Self-hosted, not a LocalAI cloud.

title: Ollama
blurb: Open-source local runner that pulls a model and serves it. The model license is still the license of the weights you pull.

title: Open WebUI
blurb: Open web interface commonly sat in front of Ollama. A UI, not a model.

title: llm
blurb: Simon Willison's CLI for calling models, with plugins for local backends. A client, not a weight file.

title: textgen
blurb: Open-source desktop app for local LLMs. The old text-generation-webui URL redirects here.

title: BitNet
blurb: Microsoft's 1-bit LLM inference code. A research runtime for ternary and bitnet-style models, not a general GGUF server.

title: Cactus
blurb: Edge inference stack named in the Gemma 4 launch as a day-one target. Open code for running small models off-server.

title: ExecuTorch
blurb: PyTorch's on-device runtime. Used to ship small open models onto phones, not to serve a 70B.

title: LiteRT-LM
blurb: Google's edge LLM runtime, the path Gemma documents for on-device runs.

title: MLX-VLM
blurb: Vision-language inference on Apple MLX. The text-only path is mlx-lm; this is the multimodal one.

title: Transformers.js
blurb: Runs Hub models in the browser and Node through ONNX. Practical for small open models, not frontier MoEs.

title: nanoGPT
blurb: Andrej Karpathy's small, readable GPT trainer. A teaching codebase, not a cluster stack.

title: llm.c
blurb: Training a GPT in plain C and CUDA, for people who want the kernels without a framework.

title: llama2.c
blurb: One-file C inference for a Llama 2 architecture. A teaching runtime, not a serving stack.

title: nanochat
blurb: Karpathy's later minimal stack that trains a small chat model end to end, including the tokenization and the fine-tune.

title: modded-nanogpt
blurb: A speedrun of nanoGPT: the same small training task, with the tricks that actually cut the wall-clock time.

title: Megatron-LM
blurb: NVIDIA's large-model training library. The code many cluster pretrains still fork.

title: LLM Foundry
blurb: Mosaic's training recipes on top of Composer. Open pretraining code; the Composer org is now part of Databricks.

title: MaxText
blurb: JAX reference trainer for LLMs on Google's accelerator stack. Open code, not a Gemma weight.

title: Levanter
blurb: JAX trainer used by the Marin open-model effort. The stanford-crfm/levanter URL redirects here.

title: Lingua
blurb: Meta's research training codebase for language models. Open code; it does not relicense Llama weights.

title: nanotron
blurb: Hugging Face's small 3D-parallelism trainer. A research pretraining stack, lighter than Megatron.

title: LitGPT
blurb: Lightning's readable implementation of open model architectures, with pretrain and fine-tune recipes.

title: TorchTitan
blurb: PyTorch's reference distributed trainer for large language models.

title: DeepSpeed
blurb: Microsoft's distributed training library, ZeRO included. The microsoft/DeepSpeed URL redirects here.

title: Mamba
blurb: State-space model code, an alternative to the Transformer used by almost everything else in this list.

title: TRL
blurb: Hugging Face's library for SFT, DPO, PPO, and related post-training. The default open alignment toolkit.

title: PEFT
blurb: Parameter-efficient fine-tunes, LoRA included, for open checkpoints.

title: Accelerate
blurb: Hugging Face's device and distributed launcher. Most of the fine-tune tools here sit on it.

title: Alignment Handbook
blurb: Recipes that reproduce known chat and preference fine-tunes with TRL. A cookbook, not a new algorithm.

title: Axolotl
blurb: YAML-driven fine-tune runner used widely on open models. The OpenAccess-AI-Collective URL redirects here.

title: Unsloth
blurb: Fine-tune library that patches kernels to use less memory. Open code aimed at LoRA on open weights.

title: LLaMA-Factory
blurb: Web and CLI fine-tune tool for a long list of open models. The LLaMA-Factory spelling redirects here.

title: ms-swift
blurb: ModelScope's fine-tune toolkit, commonly used on Qwen and other open checkpoints.

title: torchtune
blurb: PyTorch-native post-training library. The pytorch/torchtune URL redirects here.

title: OpenRLHF
blurb: Open RLHF stack for preference optimization at scale. Built for open weights, not a closed API.

title: verl
blurb: RL post-training framework (HybridFlow). The volcengine/verl URL redirects here.

title: open-instruct
blurb: AllenAI's post-training recipes, including the Tulu line. Fully open fine-tunes, with the data releases that go with them.

title: Open R1
blurb: Hugging Face's open reproduction of the DeepSeek-R1 training recipe. Code and notes, not a claim of identical weights.

title: QLoRA
blurb: The original QLoRA code: 4-bit base weights plus LoRA. The paper's repo, still the reference implementation.

title: FSDP QLoRA
blurb: Answer.AI's code for QLoRA under FSDP, which is how people fine-tune larger open models on more than one GPU.

title: mistral-finetune
blurb: Mistral's reference fine-tune code for its open models.

title: distilabel
blurb: Synthetic-data and preference-data pipeline. Open code for building the sets the fine-tune tools consume.

title: NeMo-Aligner
blurb: NVIDIA's alignment toolkit (SFT, RLHF, DPO) for its training stack. The NeMo GitHub name now redirects to a speech repo, so this is the alignment link.

title: Llama Cookbook
blurb: Meta's Llama recipes for inference, fine-tuning, and RAG. The meta-llama/llama-cookbook URL redirects here. Recipes, not a new license.

title: FlashAttention
blurb: The fused attention kernel most open training and serving stacks optionally bind. A kernel repo, not a model.

title: bitsandbytes
blurb: 8-bit and 4-bit optimizers and quantization used by QLoRA and a lot of Hugging Face fine-tunes.

title: Liger Kernel
blurb: Triton kernels that drop memory use in open-model training.

title: Triton
blurb: OpenAI's compiler for writing GPU kernels in Python. Underneath many of the kernels above.

title: FlashMLA
blurb: DeepSeek's Multi-head Latent Attention kernel. Open code that goes with the V2-and-later architecture.

title: DeepEP
blurb: DeepSeek's expert-parallelism communication library. Training infrastructure published with the MoE line.

title: Arena
blurb: Blind human-preference leaderboard. The lmarena.ai URL redirects here. Open and closed models share the board; read the license column before treating a rank as an open-weight result.

title: Arena leaderboard Space
blurb: Hugging Face Space for the Arena board. The older chatbot-arena-leaderboard path redirects here.

title: Artificial Analysis
blurb: Independent index of model quality, speed, and price. Includes open-weight models and says when a number is the vendor's.

title: Open LLM Leaderboard
blurb: Hugging Face Space for the Open LLM Leaderboard. A reproducible eval board for open models; check the Space for whether a given week is still updating.

title: HELM
blurb: Stanford's Holistic Evaluation of Language Models. A broad eval suite, not a single score.

title: SWE-bench
blurb: Real GitHub-issue benchmark for coding agents. The princeton-nlp URL redirects here. Used on open code models as well as closed ones.

title: LiveCodeBench
blurb: Contamination-resistant coding benchmark that keeps adding problems after models are trained.

title: EvalPlus
blurb: Stricter HumanEval and MBPP tests. A code-eval harness, not a leaderboard vendor.

title: BigCode Evaluation Harness
blurb: BigCode's fork of the eval harness aimed at code models, including StarCoder.

title: AlpacaEval
blurb: Automatic instruction-following eval. Cheap and gameable; useful as a regression check, not as a ranking of record.

title: Arena-Hard-Auto
blurb: Automatic proxy for Arena hard prompts. A benchmark repo from the Arena authors, not the human board itself.

title: Hallucination Leaderboard
blurb: Vectara's public board for summarization hallucinations. A narrow task, which is why it is still useful.

title: Humanity's Last Exam
blurb: The HLE benchmark repo from the Center for AI Safety. A hard closed-book exam used on both open and closed models.

title: simple-evals
blurb: OpenAI's small eval set, including GPQA and MMLU variants. Open code; it does not make the target model open.

title: lm-evaluation-harness
blurb: EleutherAI's eval harness. The one open-model papers still mean when they say they ran the standard suite.

title: LightEval
blurb: Hugging Face's eval runner, used by the Open LLM Leaderboard and by groups who do not want to fork the Eleuther harness.

title: OLMES
blurb: AllenAI's standardized eval setup for OLMo and other open models. The point is a fixed protocol, not a new test set.

title: Inspect
blurb: UK AI Security Institute's eval framework. Open harness for writing task-based evals, including tool-use.

title: Attention Is All You Need
blurb: Vaswani et al., 2017. The Transformer paper. Not an open-weight release; the architecture under every model in this list.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
blurb: The GPT-3 paper. The weights were not released; it is here because the open GPT-Neo line was a response to that fact.

title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
blurb: Kaplan et al. on loss versus compute. The plot people still argue with, including the later Chinchilla correction.

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
blurb: The Chinchilla paper. Why later open models spent tokens, not just parameters.

title: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback
blurb: InstructGPT. Closed weights; the reason the open chat models exist as a category.

title: LoRA
blurb: Hu et al. on low-rank adaptation. The method behind most open fine-tunes.

title: QLoRA
blurb: Dettmers et al. Fine-tuning a quantized open model on one GPU.

title: Direct Preference Optimization
blurb: The DPO paper. The preference method implemented in TRL and most open alignment recipes.

title: ORPO
blurb: Odds-ratio preference optimization without a reference model. One of the post-DPO methods open recipes actually ship.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
blurb: The LLaMA paper. The models were a gated research release; the paper is the architecture and data description.

title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
blurb: The Llama 2 paper, including the community license discussion. Read it next to the license file, not instead of it.

title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
blurb: The Llama 3 paper. Covers the open-weight 3.1 models, not Llama 4.

title: Mixtral of Experts
blurb: The Mixtral paper. Sparse MoE details for the Apache-2.0 8x7B model.

title: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
blurb: Architecture and training report for DeepSeek-V3. The weight license is the one in the repo, not this PDF.

title: DeepSeek-R1
blurb: The R1 technical report: reasoning trained on the V3 base, with MIT weights and distilled smaller models.

title: Olmo 3
blurb: The Olmo 3 paper. Fully open 7B and 32B models, including the model-flow claim.

title: The RefinedWeb Dataset
blurb: Falcon's public web dataset paper. A pretraining-data release, which is rarer than a weight release.

title: DCLM
blurb: DataComp for language models. An open data-curation result, with a public baseline corpus.

title: Tulu 3
blurb: AllenAI's open post-training recipe and the evals that go with it.

title: Open Source AI Definition
blurb: The OSI's definition. The line this list uses between Apache-or-MIT and a custom weight license.

title: The Illustrated Transformer
blurb: Jay Alammar's walkthrough of the architecture. Still the clearest single picture.

title: The Bitter Lesson
blurb: Rich Sutton's essay on general methods that scale. Background, not a model release.

title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
blurb: Lilian Weng's 2023 survey of agent patterns. The diagram people still copy.

title: Patterns for Building LLM Systems
blurb: Eugene Yan's notes on production LLM patterns. Pairs with his open-llm index.

title: Interconnects
blurb: Nathan Lambert's newsletter. The open-model and post-training coverage is the reason it is here.

title: Latent Space
blurb: Swyx and Alessio's podcast and newsletter. Interviews and paper walkthroughs, not a benchmark.

title: Simon Willison's weblog
blurb: Running notes on local models and the tools around them, usually with the command he actually typed.

title: Hugging Face blog
blurb: First-party write-ups when a weight release lands on the Hub, including the DeepSeek-V4 post linked above.

title: Hugging Face Llama 3 blog
blurb: How Llama 3 was wired into the Hub and the open fine-tune tools on release day. A practical companion to Meta's post.

title: You can now train a 70b language model at home
blurb: Answer.AI's FSDP-QLoRA write-up. The code is the fsdp_qlora repo in the training section.

title: The Pile
blurb: EleutherAI's 800GB public corpus, the pretraining set for the early Pythia and GPT-NeoX models.

title: RedPajama
blurb: Together's open reproduction of the Llama training mix. A dataset project, not a model.

title: RefinedWeb
blurb: TII's filtered web dataset, released with the Falcon models. The paper is in the evals section.

title: FineWeb
blurb: Hugging Face's large cleaned web corpus. The common public pretraining set after RefinedWeb.

title: FineWeb-Edu
blurb: The education-filtered slice of FineWeb. Smaller, and what a lot of small-model recipes actually train on.

title: DCLM baseline
blurb: The public baseline corpus from the DCLM paper. A data-curation result you can download.

title: Dolma
blurb: AllenAI's open corpus toolkit and data, the pretraining source for OLMo.

title: The Stack v2
blurb: BigCode's code corpus for StarCoder2. Software-license filtered, which is why it is not 'all of GitHub'.

title: UltraChat 200k
blurb: A 200k-scale chat set used in open SFT recipes. Synthetic user-assistant turns, not human preference data.

title: LMSYS-Chat-1M
blurb: A million real conversations collected by LMSYS. Human prompts, with the privacy processing described on the card.

title: OpenHermes 2.5
blurb: A widely reused synthetic instruction set. High signal as a historical SFT mix, not as a current frontier recipe.

title: Tulu 3 SFT mixture
blurb: The supervised-fine-tune mix from the Tulu 3 paper. Public post-training data with a paper attached.

title: Magpie
blurb: Generates instruction data from an aligned model without a human seed set. A method and a code release.

title: datatrove
blurb: Hugging Face's library for filtering and deduplicating large text corpora. The tool behind FineWeb-style pipelines.

title: open-llms
blurb: Eugene Yan's table of open LLMs with licenses and sizes. An index this list consulted, not a mirror of it.

title: Awesome-LLM
blurb: A broad awesome list of LLM papers, tools, and models. Much wider than open weights.

title: LLM Course
blurb: Maxime Labonne's course-shaped list of LLM papers and tooling, with a bias toward things you can run.

title: Awesome LLM resources
blurb: A large Chinese-and-English bookmark list of LLM papers and repos. An index, not a curated open-weight catalog.

title: Awesome Transformer NLP
blurb: Older awesome list of Transformer papers and code. Useful history, not a 2026 model picker.

title: awesome-llm-os
blurb: A list about LLMs as operating systems. A different topic from this repo; linked so the names are not confused.

title: EleutherAI
blurb: The research group behind GPT-Neo, Pythia, the Pile, and the eval harness. Still the closest thing to an institution for open model science.

title: Hugging Face Hub
blurb: Where the weight files, dataset cards, and licenses actually live. A model is not 'released' for this list until it is here or in a vendor repo.

title: Hugging Face Discord
blurb: The public Discord invite for the Hub. Model-specific channels move; this is the front door.

title: llama.cpp discussions
blurb: The practical forum for GGUF, quants, and 'does this checkpoint run'. More useful than a general chat room if you are serving locally.
